items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: [sings melody of Stardust] Jack Jenney and Jack Teagarden were those kind of players. Wonderful trombone players. Tommy Dorsey in his day was, perfected that original legato style, it was square but boy did he play well, whooph! And he got a sound out of the instrument that wouldn’t quit, but for jazz trombone players I guess there were, there’s Jimmy Harrison, Jack Teagarden was probably the great white trombone player of the 20s and 30s.
And Jack Jenney. Miff Mole, great, terribly underrated. Then I guess, Tricky Sam, Lawrence Brown, you know all of Ellington’s guys, Dicky Wells, wonderful player.
